what: Complaints already read for this map that are not inside any case, where the office recorded harm on the ground or found the lender out of compliance. These are the leads the complaint registers themselves hold.

source.note: Built from window.CMP in base.html on 11 Nov 2026, which holds all 3,001 complaints published by the fourteen offices on this map. 2,257 of them sit in no case; these are the ones that carry a harm record or a non-compliance finding. Each row keeps the office's own wording and its own URL.

leads.title: Ha Mpiti–Sehlabathebe road workers
leads.alleged: Workers of CNQC struck in 2021 over unpaid lockdown wages, missing payslips and unsafe truck transport; a woman was injured falling from a truck. China Eximbank lent RMB 700 million.
leads.findings: AidData records the Chinese financing and summarizes press and NGO reports of harm; it makes no finding of its own.
leads.why: the office or another source recorded harm on the ground, and no case on this map covers it

leads.title: Transmission Line IV, Ngäbe-Buglé, Panama
leads.alleged: Indigenous community members said the planned power line would displace them and destroy nature and livelihoods, and that they were not properly consulted.
leads.findings: CAO found IFC's advice left several Indigenous communities out of the consent process and said this contributed to harm. ETESA ignored the advice and dropped the line in 2025; CAO closed project-level monitoring in 2026, one IFC-wide action still open.

leads.key: cao:Myanmar: Myanma Awba Group Company Ltd.-01/Myanmar
leads.title: Awba agrochemical plant, Hmawbi, Myanmar
leads.alleged: Villagers said the new pesticide plant affected creeks and wells, that they were not consulted, and that workers at the old state plant next door had health problems.
leads.findings: CAO found IFC out of compliance. Pollution claims could not be verified for lack of data, but lack of disclosure and engagement harmed the complainants. Monitoring continues.

leads.key: cao:Egypt: Egyptian Indian Polyester Company Sokhna-01/Hyderabad
leads.title: EIPET plastics plant severance, Ain Sokhna, Egypt
leads.alleged: Former workers said the company did not pay their full salaries and severance when their contracts ended.
leads.findings: The company did not dispute that it owed the money. After CAO-assisted talks, its majority shareholder paid everything owed in 2017 and the case closed.

leads.title: Bidco factory workers, Thika, Kenya
leads.alleged: Current and former workers at the Thika plant raised concerns about job terms, safety, union rights and treatment of casual workers.
leads.findings: CAO investigated. It found IFC had not ensured casual workers' termination pay met Kenyan law, noting Bidco had lost several court cases brought by such workers, and lacked assurance on safety. Monitoring of one IFC-wide action continues.

leads.title: Sabah Forest Industries union, Sipitang, Malaysia

leads.findings: CAO investigated and found IFC's review and supervision fell short and contributed to adverse outcomes for the workers. IFC took no project action; closed in 2020.

leads.title: Binga dam, Benguet, Philippines
leads.alleged: Ibaloi residents displaced by the original dams over 50 years ago sought redress for lost land and livelihoods, plus jobs, when the plants were privatised.
leads.findings: CAO ran a dialogue. In 2009 the parties signed an agreement on land use, local benefits and jobs; CAO monitored it for a year and closed the case.

leads.title: Diamond exploration, Central Kalahari, Botswana

leads.findings: CAO found the San were removed by a government policy unrelated to the exploration, which did not disrupt their way of life. Closed in 2006.

leads.title: Pune Metro Rail Project

leads.title: Toll plaza on NH-730C, Farrukhabad, India
leads.alleged: 109 villagers said a toll plaza moved into their market would block shops, homes and two school gates used by about 367 students, without consultation.
leads.findings: Management admitted lapses. The toll plaza was moved and six actions fixed residual harms, including blocked access and three damaged water pumps. The requesters were satisfied; the Panel recommended no investigation and the Board agreed in July 2026.
leads.why: the office or another source recorded harm on the ground, and no case on this map covers it

leads.title: Raw sewage in Swarn Rekha river, Gwalior, India (second request)
leads.alleged: Two Gwalior residents said a sewer line crushed during river lining work left raw sewage flowing, causing illness such as malaria and dengue for many people.
leads.findings: The Panel saw raw sewage in the river affecting many residents, but found no credible link to the Bank-financed river lining. With the first request, it recommended no investigation.
leads.why: the office or another source recorded harm on the ground, and no case on this map covers it

leads.title: Quilleco hydropower plant, Biobío, Chile
leads.alleged: Residents of Tucapel, Santa Bárbara, Ralco Lepoy and Concepción, including Pehuenche representatives, said World Bank Group–backed dams on the Laja and Biobío rivers had harmed and would harm their region.
leads.findings: The Panel found the plant sharply cut flow in a stretch of the Laja River and that lost island fertility had badly hurt livelihoods, but traced that loss mainly to an earlier dam. It recommended no investigation in August 2011.
leads.why: the office or another source recorded harm on the ground, and no case on this map covers it

leads.title: Bus rapid transit, Barranco, Lima, Peru
leads.alleged: Barranco residents said the bus corridor was built without consultation or proper study and damaged their neighborhood and its historic buildings.
leads.findings: The Panel investigated. It found poorly managed traffic changes lowered many residents' quality of life, and the Bank out of compliance on study and consultation.
leads.why: the office or another source recorded harm on the ground, and no case on this map covers it

leads.title: Water hyacinth shredding, Lake Victoria, Kenya
leads.alleged: A Kenyan NGO said shredding water hyacinth and sinking it in the lake would pollute the Nyanza Gulf and harm lakeshore people who depend on it for fish and water.
leads.findings: The Panel investigated and found a serious lack of attention to the science behind the shredding pilot, and the Bank out of compliance on environmental assessment, including consultation, and on supervision.

leads.title: Metro of Bogota First Line - First Tranch — Request IV

The Requester alleges an incorrect appraisal of his property, since the amount offered would be less than an appraisal cited by the Requester.
leads.findings: The case was closed with the full implementation of six agreements. It was the first occasion in which a MICI complaint generated multiple separate agreements to address the specific circumstances of each requester and restore their living conditions affected by the resettlement of their homes or businesses.

leads.key: ncp:Employees of Kawaguchi Manufacturing vs. Kawaguchi Manufacturing, Sony and Panasonic
leads.title: Labour rights violations at supplier to Sony and Panasonic
leads.alleged: On 27 December 2024, 251 workers of Kawaguchi Manufacturing Sdn. Bhd. (“Kawaguchi Manufacturing”), represented by lawyers, filed a complaint against Kawaguchi Manufacturing, Sony Corporation (“Sony”) and Panasonic Corporation (“Panasonic”) at the Japanese NCP. The complaint concerns alleged labour rights violations at Kawaguchi Manufacturing in Malaysia and their links to Sony and Panasonic.
leads.findings: On 27 June 2025 and 17 July 2025, Sony and Panasonic respectively submitted statements to the Japanese NCP in mid-2025 explaining their due diligence policies and actions in relation to the issues raised in the complaint. On 24 April 2026, the Japanese NCP issued its Final Statement detailing the above developments.

leads.key: ncp:Workers of Pharmakina vs. Schweppes Holdings Ireland
leads.title: Workers’ rights and other violations in Democratic Republic of the Congo linked to quinine supply chain
leads.alleged: Workers dismissed by the quinine-producing company Pharmakina, S.A. in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) submitted a complaint to the Luxembourg NCP arguing that Pharmakina S.A. and its Luxembourg-incorporated holding company, Pharmeg S.A., had breached the OECD Guidelines Employment and Industrial Relations, Human Rights, and other chapters when it fired workers seeking to be paid a legal wage.
leads.findings: According to complainants, while the complaint to the Luxembourg NCP was underway, Pharmakina sought the arrest of one of the worker representatives. The Irish NCP rejected the complaint, asserting the complainants had not provided sufficient evidence to link the company to the business enterprise (Pharmakina) and to the impacts alleged by the complainants.

leads.key: ncp:Workers of Pharmakina vs. Pharmakina S.A., Pharmeg S.A.

leads.key: ncp:Committee Seeking Justice for Alethankyaw vs. Telenor
leads.title: Telenor due diligence in Myanmar
leads.alleged: On 16 December 2019, the Committee Seeking Justice for Alethankyaw (CSJA) filed a specific instance against Telenor at the Norwegian NCP. The NCP also recommended enterprises operating in conflict situations take note of the report of the UN Working Group on Business and Human Rights on conflict-affected regions and states, in…

leads.key: ncp:Canada Tibet Committee vs. China Gold Int. Resources
leads.title: Environmental, HR & disclosure issues China Gold Int.

leads.findings: After confirming receipt on 28 January, CTC did not hear from the NCP until 17 April, when the NCP informed CTC that China Gold was unwilling to engage in the process despite multiple requests from the NCP. leads.key: ncp:PWT Group’s role in the Rana Plaza collapse

leads.findings: The Danish NCP accepted the case on 2 February 2015 and encouraged the parties to resolve the matter themselves, but as the parties did not wish to resolve it on their own, the Danish NCP completed its initial assessment and offered the parties mediation assisted by the NCP. leads.key: ncp:Thai and Filipino labour unions vs Triumph International
leads.title: Labour rights at Triumph Thai & Philippine garment factories
leads.alleged: A coalition of labour unions, NGOs and labour support groups filed a complaint against Swiss undergarment manufacturer Triumph International for carrying out massive layoffs without consulting unions in Thailand and the Philippines. In August 2009, nearly 2,000 workers were suddenly retrenched at the companys Thai factory, cutting the factorys workforce in half.
leads.findings: The Swiss NCP accepted the case as a specific instance in February 2010 and then proceeded to consult with the parties to establish the terms for handling the case. In its final statement, the NCP does not make any assessment of whether Triumphs actions were in breach of the OECD Guidelines , nor does it make recommendations to enhance implementation of the Guidelines.

leads.title: Bayer’s cotton seed production in India
